question.problem: What is the coefficient of $(x-\pi )^{2}$ in the second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$ at $x=\pi ?$
question.worked_solution:
The second-degree Taylor polynomial of $f(x)$ about $x=\pi $ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{P}_{2}(x) & =f(\pi )+{f}^{′}(\pi )(x-\pi )+\frac{{f}^{″}(\pi )}{2}(x-\pi )^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

The coefficient of $(x-\pi )^{2}$ in the above Taylor polynomial is 

$$
\frac{1}{2}{f}^{″}(\pi ).
$$

To find this coefficient, we start by computing the second derivative ${f}^{″}(x):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡x \\ {f}^{″}(x) & =-\operatorname{cos}⁡x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we evaluate ${f}^{″}(x)$ at $x=\pi .$ This gives

$$
{f}^{″}(\pi )=-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\pi )=-(-1)=1.
$$

Finally, we determine the coefficient of $(x-\pi )^{2},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{f}^{″}(\pi )}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$
